## 4 Determination of the electrical parameters

Looking at (1) gives us the needed electrical parameters to be defined. We find R and L, the resistance and the inductance of the coil, Uf; the force constant, and Ubemfs the bemf (back electromagnetic   force) constant of the system.

R and L are the intrinsic electrical properties of the coil and are purely passive. A simple measurement on the RLC meter will allow us to get those values. These are given in Table 3

The quantities uf and Ubemf are representative of the same phenomenon the expression of the Lorentz force but have neither the same causes nor the same effects .

Lorentz expresses that the charge carriers of a conductor immersed in a (non-collinear) magnetic field are subjected to a force when moving and this according to the following relation:

With Fq the force   exerted on carrier of electrical 9 subjected to an electric field E, undergoing a v, and immersed in a magnetic field B charge charge speed

The   generalized expression of this force on conductor of length / is:

The current flowing in the coil generates a force F on the latter with respect to the force constant uf:

The magnitude   Ubemf expresses the force undergone by the electrons in conductor which moves in magnetic field. The displacement of the coil generates an electric potential at the conductor terminals with respect to the bemf constant\_

We study a system which on the one hand generates force due to an applied current and on the other hand which creates an electrical potential with respect to the of the coil. This approach forms the basis of the development   of two-port network model and goes beyond the scope of this work. Different authors such as York, Smallwood or Guillaume   develop this   aspect deeper in detail [11-13] speed

## 4.1 Experimental determination of the force constant

First; we used the assembly already presented in Figure 3 which blocks the vibrating table. A voltage is to the terminals which generates current, which creates a force. Due to the rigid structure, the table cannot move and no bemf can settle. applied

A measurement of the force with   respect to the current yields the force constant. The latter is shown in Figure 9 for three different drive voltages.

We immediately notice very strong structural response at 660 Hz due to the resonance of the structure originally intended to be rigid. By performing modal analysis structure, we obtained its   frequency response. The synthesized curve has been superimposed on the measured curves to emphasize the response due to the resonance of the beam structure.

Fig. 9. Force Constant analysis for different drive voltages. The synthesized FRF of the beam structure is superimposed on the measured curves to emphasize the response due to the resonance of the beam structure.

<!-- image -->

Beyond this, the measurements tend to show an increase in damping with the drive voltage underlying a possible non-linearity of the system.

At this any deduction is dangerous and should be avoided. Further analysis is required . Nevertheless; in the area below 100 the relative theoretical error due to the resonating structure with respect to the unity does not exceed 3%. Despite relative variation in amplitude of 5% over the frequencies, the value of uf is considered to be constant.   Its average value is 7.8493 NIA an initial value form the manufacturer of 6.4 NIA. These data are shown in Table 3 point Hz; against
